raw_response:
I've been working this land for 40 years. I know Quzhou well — the springs are dry, summers bring some rain but not always enough, and the wells are what keep us going. My wife and I can handle 8 mu between the two of us, though it gets harder at my age.

**Maize — my main crop.** I'll put 6 mu into spring maize, plant late April when the soil warms. I switched to hybrid seeds maybe 20 years ago. Everyone around here uses them now — Zhengdan 958 or whatever the seed shop has that year. Better grain, better yield. I'll spread compound fertilizer at planting, then come back with urea when the stalks are knee-high. With the well, I pump 4 times — once before planting to wet the bed, twice through June when it's dry, and once more in August if the ears look thirsty. Corn borer is always a problem here, so I spray 3 times: herbicide early, then insecticide twice as the season goes on.

**Mungbean — 2 mu, keeps us some cash.** I use seeds saved from last year's harvest, the same local type my family has grown for generations. Mungbean doesn't need much — the roots take care of some of the nitrogen themselves. I fertilize lightly, water twice or three times, and watch for aphids. One or two sprays usually handles it.

Tillage I do with the rotary machine, same as always. No reason to change what works.
